comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C10, C11, C49, C50, C63 regarding epistasis experiments showing pC1d-aIPg recurrent connectivity is not required for persistent aggression. Both evaluations find this negative result convincing and well-supported by the data.

Strong agreement on claims C6, C7, C35, C38, C62, C71, C75, C76 regarding synergistic effects of pC1d+e co-stimulation producing persistent aggression. Both evaluations treat this as a key finding showing emergent circuit properties, with OpenEval providing additional detail on the inference of synergy and pC1e's modulatory role.

Strong agreement on claims C8, C51, C52, C54, C56, C64, C69, C70 regarding calcium imaging showing no persistent neural activity despite persistent behavior. Both evaluations accept this mismatch as well-supported, though OpenEval notes potential limitations of head-fixed preparations while peer reviewers do not raise this concern.

Agreement on claims C3, C34, C37, C55, C60 regarding aIPg stimulation producing persistent aggression. Both evaluations affirm this core finding. OpenEval additionally discusses claims C4, C36, C103, C104 about experimental design and differential effects, which peer reviewers address separately in R2.

Partial overlap on claims C4, C36 regarding pC1d alone not producing persistent aggression. OpenEval groups this with aIPg findings in R1, while peer reviewers treat it as a separate result in R2. Both evaluations support the finding without concerns.

Agreement on claim C74 regarding the conceptual distinction between time-locked and persistent control of aggression. Both evaluations treat this as an important interpretive conclusion supported by the differential behavioral effects. OpenEval also includes C73 in this evaluation.

Agreement on claims C20, C53, C65, C66, C67 regarding connectomic data from hemibrain dataset. Both evaluations accept this anatomical foundation without concerns. OpenEval additionally discusses claims C78, C79, C91-C95 about specific circuit details and visual inputs, which peer reviewers do not explicitly address.

Agreement on claims C57, C58 regarding the inference that recurrent connectivity is not the mechanism for persistent aggression. Both evaluations support this conclusion based on combined behavioral and imaging data. OpenEval additionally discusses claims C9, C59, C68, with C59 also appearing in peer R10.

Agreement on claims C47, C48 regarding density effects on persistence duration. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this supporting data without explicit discussion, while OpenEval notes the lack of detailed statistical analysis in supplementary figures. OpenEval additionally discusses claims C40-C42, C44-C46 not explicitly addressed by peer reviewers.

Partial overlap on claim C59 regarding speculation about downstream mechanisms. OpenEval treats this as a reasonable but untested inference in the context of ruling out recurrent connectivity (R6), while peer reviewers accept it as a logical direction for future work (R10).

Partial overlap on claim C82 regarding speculative mechanisms. OpenEval rates R11 as UNCERTAIN, noting these are untested hypotheses rather than supported findings (C82-C86). Peer reviewers in R10 implicitly accept such speculation as reasonable future directions, treating it more favorably.

OpenEval evaluates claims C22-C33 regarding accurate summarization of prior work and its limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these background claims, though peer R8 briefly mentions prior connectomics work.

OpenEval evaluates claims C77, C80, C81 regarding visual inputs to pC1e and comparisons to male pCd neurons. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these connectomic inferences and contextualizations.

OpenEval evaluates claims C101, C102, C105 regarding behavioral analysis methods and classifier performance. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these methodological details, though they underlie all behavioral findings.
